C0.quote: we take a social choice approach and compare 5 different axis selection rules
C0.note: Rules aggregating voters' approval ballots into a collective ordering (axis).

C1.loc: Abstract and Section 5, p. 2757; Theorem 1, p. 2760; Section 6, pp. 2762–2763
C1.quote: compare 5 different axis selection rules axiomatically, by studying the properties they satisfy
C1.note: Axiomatic analysis (Sections 4–5), NP-completeness (Theorem 1), synthetic simulations (Section 6.1), real datasets (Sections 6.2–6.3).

C2.1.quote: An approval ballot is a non-empty subset of candidates

C2.2.quote: An approval ballot is a non-empty subset of candidates

C2.3.quote: Each candidate and voter x ∈ C ∪ V is associated with a position
C2.3.note: In the synthetic noisy observation model, voters hold positions/ideal points; main model has only ballots.

C2.4.quote: Voters approve (resp. rank) candidates based on their estimations
C2.4.note: Only in the synthetic experiment: ballots are noisy observations of position-based approvals, modelled separately from held positions. Main analyses treat ballots as given data with no held attitude.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers voters submitting ballots differing from any held attitude; ballots are taken as exogenous data.

C3.2.note: No statement of sincere voting or that ballots equal held attitudes.

C4.1.quote: approval set of voter v contains all candidates such that
C4.1.note: Noisy observation model defines approvals (and rankings) from voter/candidate positions; also MLE interpretation in Section 3. Applicable since APPR input and utility notions ('random utility models') are used.

C4.2.note: Term 'dichotomous preferences' appears only in cited reference titles, not used in the text.

C5.1.note: Axioms concern axis structure (stability, monotonicity, clones), not voter welfare, efficiency, representation or distortion.

VOT.quote_behav: An approval profile P is a collection of n approval ballots
VOT.note: Voters' ballots are fixed exogenous inputs; no strategic choice modelled.

CAN.note: Candidates are only alternatives being ordered.

C7.1.note: Only one type (VOT) present, and non-strategic.

C8.1.note: No type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: Our rules will find an axis in a principled way.

C9.1.note: Also framed against pollsters who 'construct ad hoc' axes for real French elections.

C9.2.note: Claim that the rules yield principled ideological axes for real elections needs the assumption that submitted approval ballots correspond to voters' ideological positions/preferences; no such relation is stated (the paper even notes ballots may be shaped by incomplete knowledge, Section 4, p. 2760).

C10.1.note: No explicit procedural statement; rules are applied to approval profiles as given data throughout.
